meta.title: Costa Nativa — Architect-designed house with private pool, Brasilito, Guanacaste
meta.description: A calm two-bedroom house with a private pool, set in five thousand square metres of Guanacaste forest, eight hundred metres from Playa Brasilito. Sleeps five. Book on Airbnb.
meta.ogAlt: Costa Nativa at dusk, the lit pool reflecting the open living space

hero.title: A house that opens to the trees.
hero.subtitle: Two bedrooms, a private pool, and five thousand square metres of forest — eight hundred metres from Playa Brasilito.

opening.body:
There is a moment, usually on the second morning, when you stop reaching for your phone. The house is quiet except for the birds. The doors are already open — they tend to stay open here — and the pool is holding the shape of the trees above it.

That is what Costa Nativa is for.

house.title: Open, and then more open.
house.body: The main living space has no hard edge. Sliding walls fold back until the kitchen, the sofa and the terrace are a single room and the breeze moves through all of it. The ceilings are high, light arrives from three sides, and nothing is closed off unless you decide it should be.

alt.kitchenLivingWide: The open-plan kitchen and living area, with a white quartz island, wooden cabinetry and a large framed artwork on the far wall
alt.livingToEntry: The living room looking toward the kitchen and the solid wood front door, with artworks either side of the television
alt.livingPoolView: The living room with the sliding walls drawn back, opening onto the terrace and pool beyond

pool.title: The centre of the day.
pool.body: The pool sits in the shade of the trees, a few steps from the dining table and the grill. Mornings are for coffee out here. Afternoons are for not moving very much. After dark the water lights up and the terrace quietly becomes the best room in the house.

alt.poolDay: The turquoise mosaic pool in daylight, with the covered terrace, dining table and kitchen visible beyond
alt.terraceNight: The terrace at night, the pool lit blue, with lounge seating, a long wooden dining table and framed artworks on the wall
alt.terraceWide: The full width of the covered terrace, with a gas grill, a six-seat dining table and a blue outdoor sofa

rooms.title: Built for sleeping well.
rooms.body: A king bed in the main room, a queen and a single in the second. Both have blackout shades, noise insulation and air conditioning, and both are made up with premium cotton linens. Two full bathrooms. Five people, comfortably.
rooms.bedroomTwo: Second bedroom — queen bed and single bed

alt.bedroomKing: The main bedroom with a king bed, upholstered headboard and three framed artworks above it, opening to an ensuite with a round backlit mirror
alt.bedroomTwo: The second bedroom with two beds dressed in teal, a row of small framed works on the wall and an ensuite beyond
alt.bathroom: A bathroom with a polished concrete partition, white towels and a small framed artwork

design.title: Designed, not decorated.
design.body: Costa Nativa was drawn by the Costa Rican architects Murillo + Sanabria in 2021, around a private collection of work by the artist Jacques Hervot. The white walls and the plain detailing are deliberate — they are there so the paintings can speak. You will find them in every room, including the ones you would not expect.
design.alt: The covered terrace lounge, two framed works on the white wall above a blue sofa, the garden beyond

setting.title: Eight hundred metres to the water.
setting.body: Playa Brasilito is a three-minute drive — a small town square, a handful of good restaurants, boards and boat trips for hire. Playa Conchal, the one made of crushed shells, is around the headland. The house itself sits inside Catalina Cove, a gated community with round-the-clock security, on five thousand square metres of endemic Guanacaste and Brasilito trees full of birds and, most mornings, monkeys.
setting.distancesNote: Driving times are approximate and depend on the season and the road.
